item.title: The U.S. unexpectedly lost jobs in July
item.description: The U.S. labor market went into reverse last month, as employers cut 23,000 jobs. Job gains for May and June were also revised downward.
item.content:encoded: The U.S. labor market went into reverse last month, as employers cut 23,000 jobs. Job gains for May and June were also revised downward.
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: Trump renews push to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook
item.description: Trump is once again threatening to fire Cook over unproven allegations of mortgage fraud after an earlier effort to remove Cook was struck down by the Supreme Court.

item.title: Employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs in a sign of a wilting labor market
item.description: U.S. employers cut 23,000 jobs in July, and job gains for the two previous months were weaker than initially reported, according to a report Friday from the Labor Department.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. employers cut 23,000 jobs in July, and job gains for the two previous months were weaker than initially reported, according to a report Friday from the Labor Department.

(Image credit: Joe Raedle)
item.dc:creator: Scott Horsley

item.title: Amid cost of living stress, many parents are supporting children well into adulthood
item.description: Polls show most Americans think young adults today have it harder financially than past generations. A majority of parents help their grown children with expenses, even if it hurts their own finances.

item.title: U.S. economy unexpectedly loses 23,000 jobs in July
item.description: The Labor Department offered an update Friday morning on the U.S. jobs market. After lackluster hiring in June, forecasters had expected the report to show a modest pickup in July.

item.title: Oil companies report sky-high profits thanks to wartime crude prices
item.description: Chevron reported its highest quarterly earnings ever. Shell had its second-biggest quarter, and ExxonMobil doubled its earnings compared with the same time last year.

item.title: How did boosting manufacturing in the Amazon pay off for Brazil?
item.description: Many countries talk about wanting to boost manufacturing. Decades ago, Brazil did it. They lured international businesses to build a whole bunch of factories in the middle of the Amazon. So, with hindsight, was the plan a success? Planet Money goes to the Amazon to find out.
